accepted.evidence: DEDR 2559 explicitly gives Te. lēdu ‘no, none’ in the negative-existence paradigm; LSI lēdŭ is that form.
DEDR 4572 gives Te. pōvu with stems pō- and pōy- ‘go’; LSI pō is the cited short stem.
DEDR 474 explicitly gives Te. iruvadi, colloquial iruvai ‘twenty’; LSI iruvai matches the colloquial form.
DEDR 2826 gives Te. yābhai ‘fifty’; LSI yābʰai represents the same form with aspirated survey spelling.
DEDR 3647 gives Te. manamu ‘we’ with oblique mana-; LSI manā ‘our’ is an oblique possessive form of that inclusive plural pronoun.
DEDR 5154 gives Te. mēmu ‘we’ with oblique man-/mā-; LSI mā ‘our’ matches the possessive stem mā-.
DEDR 3684 explicitly gives Te. nīvu ‘thou’ with oblique nī-/nin-; LSI nīvu matches the nominative form.
DEDR 3684 gives Te. nīvu with oblique nī-/nin-; LSI nī ‘thy’ is the possessive stem nī-.
DEDR 3688 gives Te. mīru ‘you’ with oblique mī-/mim-; LSI mīru matches the cited form.
DEDR 3675 gives Te. nilucu ‘stand’ in the nil- family; LSI nilʦ is a reduced elicited stem with the same sense.
DEDR 2426 gives Te. caccu with stem cā- ‘die’; LSI ʦā is that short stem in survey transcription.
DEDR 2598 gives Te. iccu with stems ī̆-/iyy-/ivv- ‘give’; LSI iy is the short iyy- stem.
DEDR 713 gives Te. uṟuku ‘jump, run away’; LSI uruk ‘run’ matches the stem, though the survey gloss is broader.
DEDR 2063 gives Te. koṭṭu ‘beat, strike, knock’; LSI koṭṭ is the elicited verbal stem.
DEDR 3688 gives Te. mīru with oblique mī-/mim-; LSI mī ‘your’ matches the possessive stem mī-.
The full demonstrative article DEDR 1 explicitly gives Te. vā̃ḍu ‘that man, he’; LSI vāḍu matches the pronoun.
DEDR 1 explicitly gives Te. vā̃ḍu with oblique vāni-; LSI vāni ‘his’ matches that stem.
DEDR 1 explicitly gives Te. vāru ‘those persons, they’; LSI vāru matches the pronoun.
DEDR 1 explicitly gives Te. vāru with oblique vāri-; LSI vāri ‘their’ matches that stem.
DEDR 3633 gives Te. nālika/nāluka/nālka ‘tongue’; LSI nālukĕ is a survey variant of nāluka.
DEDR 486 explicitly gives Te. inumu ‘iron’; LSI inumŭ matches it.
The full DEDR 5496 white/shine article gives Te. veṇḍi ‘silver’; LSI veṇḍĭ matches that reflex.
DEDR 494 explicitly gives Te. illu ‘house, dwelling’; LSI illŭ matches it.
DEDR 1711 gives Te. guṟṟamu ‘horse’; LSI gurramŭ matches. The article raises a possible Indo-Aryan origin, which this family assignment does not settle.
DEDR 1364 explicitly gives Te. gāḍida ‘ass’; LSI gāḍidĕ matches it. The article compares Sanskrit gardabha but does not establish the immediate donor.
DEDR 4180 explicitly gives Te. pilli ‘cat’; LSI pillĭ matches it. The article also compares CDIAL *billa-, so ultimate origin remains open.
DEDR 4373 gives Te. punju ‘cock’; LSI punʣŭ matches its survey affricate spelling.
DEDR 2646 explicitly gives Te. cukka ‘star’; LSI ʦukkă matches the survey affricate spelling.

held.reason: LSI kūrʦ ‘sit’ has no direct form match in the searched DEDR articles; the stand family is semantically different.
LSI nā ‘my’ needs a first-singular pronoun article; the nearby DEDR 3647/5154 articles are plural and do not justify this assignment.
DEDR 5270 has Tamil imperative vā ‘come’ but gives Telugu vaccu (rā-); LSI Telugu vā is not established as the cited Telugu reflex.

DEDR 2023 gives Te. ceyyi ‘hand’, but LSI eheyyi has an unexplained initial e- and missing c; do not normalize it silently.
LSI pādamu ‘foot’ is likely an Indo-Aryan loan, but an immediate donor and graph parent were not verified.
LSI veṇṭruka ‘hair’ lacks a matching full DEDR article or verified immediate donor.
The similar DEDR 1198 Te. kadupu means ‘mass, multitude’, not the LSI kaḍupŭ ‘belly’; the homograph is not enough.
DEDR 5488 gives Te. ven(n)u ‘back’ and Kannada bennu, but LSI Telugu bennŭ matches the Kannada onset; the source transcription or local variant needs confirmation.
LSI baŋgāramŭ ‘gold’ has no verified immediate donor or full DEDR family.
LSI naukarŭ ‘slave’ appears to be a loan; an immediate donor for this survey form was not verified.
LSI gollavāḍŭ ‘shepherd’ appears compound or caste-based; both components and its history need verification.
LSI dēvuḍŭ ‘god’ appears to involve Sanskrit deva, but a direct immediate donor and inherited-versus-loan analysis were not established.
LSI dayyamŭ ‘devil’ lacks a verified full DEDR family or immediate donor.
LSI loṭṭipiṭṭă ‘camel’ is opaque and lacks a verified full DEDR family or immediate donor.
LSI pakṣĭ ‘bird’ likely reflects an Indo-Aryan lexeme; its immediate donor and graph parent were not established.
LSI badakŭ ‘duck’ lacks a verified full DEDR family or immediate donor.
LSI sūryuḍŭ ‘sun’ appears Indo-Aryan-derived, but its immediate donor and Telugu formation were not verified.
LSI candruḍŭ ‘moon’ appears Indo-Aryan-derived, but its immediate donor and Telugu formation were not verified.
LSI aggĭ ‘fire’ resembles Sanskrit agni but an immediate donor and Telugu sound adaptation were not verified.
